title: AI Builders Digest — 2026-11-03
subtitle: Agent 开始进入自己的工作空间，产品也开始替用户做模型选择。

intro.kicker: 今天值得读的 9 条动态
intro.text: 今天的主线很清楚：agent 不只是一个聊天窗口，它需要带着身份、skills、代码仓库和记忆进入受控的工作空间；而在专业场景里，真正有价值的产品也不再要求用户自己挑模型。与此同时，AI 产品的瓶颈越来越像是 harness、上下文和协作方式，而不只是模型本身。

archive.title: Agent 工作空间日报
archive.desc: 从受控执行环境、模型路由到专业 agent 产品，看看 AI builder 今天把注意力放在哪里。

sections.title: 01｜Agent 需要自己的工作空间
sections.desc: 从 sandbox 到 workspace，agent 的运行边界正在被重新定义。

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch argues that a stateless sandbox is the wrong benchmark for agents. An agent becomes useful when it arrives with its own workspace: identity, skills, repos, and memories.
He also points to Vercel Sandbox's reliability and security work across 19 global regions as the less glamorous infrastructure that makes agent products dependable.
original: Stateless sandboxes are the wrong benchmark. Agents are only useful if they have their workspace with them (identity, skills, repos, memories…).
Vercel Sandbox team has been beautifully delivering on their latency & throughput SLOs, while prioritizing reliability and security.

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch 认为，用无状态 sandbox 衡量 agent 是找错了指标。只有当 agent 带着自己的 workspace 一起工作——包括 identity、skills、repos 和 memories——它才真正有用。
他还提到 Vercel Sandbox 在 19 个全球区域持续做好延迟、吞吐、可靠性和安全，这些不那么性感的基础设施，才是 agent 产品能稳定运行的前提。
original: 无状态 sandbox 是错误的 benchmark。Agent 只有带着自己的 workspace 才有用。
Vercel Sandbox 团队在延迟、吞吐 SLO 的同时，优先保证可靠性和安全。

rewrite: Amjad Masad says AI agents should run in dedicated, organization-controlled environments, with access limited to the resources required for each task. The implication is practical: agent deployment needs boundaries designed into the environment, not bolted on afterward.
original: AI agents should operate in dedicated, organization-controlled environments with limited access to the resources each task requires.

rewrite: Amjad Masad 认为，AI agent 应该运行在组织自己控制的专用环境里，并且只获得完成当前任务所需的资源。换句话说，agent 的边界应该直接设计进运行环境，而不是事后补一层权限。
original: AI agent 应该运行在组织控制的专用环境中，只能访问每项任务所需的资源。

sections.title: 02｜模型选择，交给产品判断
sections.desc: 用户不想研究模型排行榜，他们只想把工作做好。

rewrite: Legora started as ChatGPT for Swedish law and grew into a legal agent that drafts, edits Word files, organizes documents, runs complex analysis, and orchestrates work between lawyers, clients, and agents.

The product team routes different parts of a task to different models. The goal is not to make lawyers choose between Sonnet and Opus; it is to keep them on the Pareto frontier while the product handles the trade-offs in cost, latency, and quality.

Lauritzen's useful dividing line is that roughly 60% of legal work is already tractable. The next frontier is less about making every answer smarter and more about cost, latency, and handling the remaining complex analysis.
original: The way everything started was ChatGPT with Swedish laws and search tool in it.
I think we found it most effective to subdivide the problem and route on, like, as we subdivide the task.
There's probably like 60% of the work we can do really well right now, and from now on, it's like a cost and latency thing.

rewrite: Legora 最初只是一个接入瑞典法律的 ChatGPT，后来成长为能起草文件、编辑 Word、整理资料、执行复杂分析，并协调律师、客户和 agent 协作的法律产品。
他们会把一个任务拆开，让不同部分使用不同模型。重点不是让律师自己在 Sonnet 和 Opus 之间做选择，而是由产品替用户处理成本、延迟和质量的取舍，让用户始终留在 Pareto frontier 上。
Lauritzen 给出的实用判断是：大约 60% 的法律工作现在已经能做得很好。下一步的关键不只是让答案更聪明，而是降低成本和延迟，并处理剩下的复杂分析。
original: 一切始于一个接入瑞典法律和搜索工具的 ChatGPT。
把问题拆开，再根据拆分后的任务进行路由，对我们最有效。
现在大约 60% 的工作已经能做得很好，接下来更多是成本和延迟问题。

rewrite: Thibault Sottiaux describes a product direction that makes model choice disappear: the user's dot chooses the best model for the task, using different models for different parts of the work. The product is becoming a routing layer, not a model picker.
original: Your dot will choose the best model for the task, drawing on different models for different parts of the work.

rewrite: Thibault Sottiaux 描述了一种让模型选择消失的产品方向：由用户的 dot 为任务选出最合适的模型，并让任务的不同部分调用不同模型。产品正在从 model picker 变成 routing layer。
original: 你的 dot 会为任务选择最佳模型，并为工作的不同部分调用不同模型。

sections.title: 03｜Harness 和协作方式才是瓶颈
sections.desc: 模型能力之外，真正影响交付速度的是工具链和多人协作结构。

rewrite: Peter Yang found that ChatGPT's writing suggestions were almost entirely bad while Gemini's were actually useful for an editing task. But the better model was held back by its harness: Antigravity did not have working browser use, so he had to paste Gemini's edits back into ChatGPT to finish the job.
The point is less about declaring a winner than about showing how product integrations can erase model quality gains.
original: The best model for writing & editing is held back by its harness.
Antigravity doesn't seem to have working browser use so I basically have to paste all of Gemini's edits back into ChatGPT to make the edits in my browser.

rewrite: Peter Yang 发现，ChatGPT 对一篇文章的改写建议几乎全都不好，而 Gemini 的建议确实有用。但更好的模型被 harness 拖住了：Antigravity 的浏览器能力还不能正常工作，他只能把 Gemini 的修改重新粘回 ChatGPT，才能在浏览器里完成编辑。
重点不只是比较谁的模型更强，而是产品集成可能直接抵消模型能力的提升。
original: 最适合写作和编辑的模型，被它的 harness 拖住了。
Antigravity 的浏览器使用似乎还不能正常工作，所以我只能把 Gemini 的所有修改粘回 ChatGPT。

rewrite: Garry Tan says Capy Captains increased his issue-fixing throughput about 5x overnight. The unlock was not a smarter single agent, but coordination across captains and subthreads.
original: Capy Captains increased my issue fixing throughput by about 5X overnight
Being able to coordinate across captains and subthreads is an insane unlock

rewrite: Garry Tan 说，Capy Captains 让他的 issue 修复吞吐量一夜之间提升了约 5 倍。关键不是单个 agent 变得更聪明，而是 captains 和 subthreads 之间可以协调起来。
original: Capy Captains 让我的 issue 修复吞吐量一夜之间提升了约 5 倍。
能够在 captains 和 subthreads 之间协调，是一个疯狂的解锁。

rewrite: Nan Yu's blunt product take: except in rare circumstances, group chat is a terrible multiplayer AI experience and is virtually guaranteed to produce slop. The lesson is that adding more participants to an AI interface does not automatically create better collaboration.
original: Except for rare circumstances, group chat is a terrible multiplayer AI experience.
Literally guaranteed slop

rewrite: Nan Yu 的判断很直接：除了少数情况，group chat 都是糟糕的多人 AI 体验，几乎注定会产出 slop。把更多参与者塞进同一个 AI 界面，并不会自动变成更好的协作。
original: 除非是少数特殊情况，group chat 都是糟糕的多人 AI 体验。
几乎注定会产出 slop。

sections.title: 04｜更便宜的智能，和更大胆的产品
sections.desc: builders 正在测试新的模型使用方式，也在重新估算智能的价格。

rewrite: After a week of using the expensive tier, Thariq's takeaway is surprisingly non-maximalist: you do not need unlimited tokens to do great work, and the $200 plans are already amazing. His sharper prediction is that this is probably the most expensive intelligence will ever be.
original: one week in my takeaway is that you don't need unlimited tokens to do great work, the $200 plans are amazing
and this is the most expensive intelligence will ever be

rewrite: Thariq 用了一周高价档之后，得出的结论并不追求极限：想把工作做好，并不需要 unlimited tokens，200 美元的套餐已经非常强。更大胆的判断是：这可能已经是智能最贵的时候。
original: 你不需要 unlimited tokens 也能做出很好的工作，200 美元的套餐已经很棒。
这会是智能最贵的时候。

rewrite: Garry Tan flags a new use for smaller models: direct manipulation of model weights. It is a compact signal that the next round of AI tooling may not only call models, but also program them at the weight level.
original: Interesting new use of smaller models: direct manipulation of weights

rewrite: Garry Tan 注意到小模型的一种新用法：直接操作模型 weights。这释放出一个简短但有意思的信号：下一轮 AI 工具不只是调用模型，也可能开始在 weight 层对模型进行编程。
original: 小模型的一个有意思的新用法：直接操作 weights。
